items.followUp: What is an anion? Give one example.

rubric.why: An ion is defined as an electrically charged atom or group of atoms.
rubric.description: Defines an ion as a charged atom or group of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an ion is a charged atom or group of atoms.

rubric.why: Cations and anions are the two types of ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both cations and anions, or both positive and negative ions.

modelAnswer: An ion is an electrically charged atom or group of atoms.
The two types of ions are cations (positive ions) and anions (negative ions).

items.followUp: What are isotopes? Explain why isotopes of an element have different mass numbers.

rubric.why: Isotopes of the same element have different numbers of neutrons.
rubric.description: Identifies the difference in neutron number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that isotopes have different numbers of neutrons.

rubric.why: The different neutron counts lead to different total atomic masses.
rubric.description: Links the neutron difference to the different atomic masses or mass numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the different neutron numbers result in different atomic masses or mass numbers.

modelAnswer: Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Since neutrons contribute to the mass of the atom, the isotopes have different atomic masses.

items.followUp: State the main idea of Dobereiner’s triads and the relationship between the atomic masses in a triad.

rubric.why: A triad is a group of three elements.
rubric.description: States that a Dobereiner triad contains three elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the group as containing three elements.

rubric.why: Dobereiner’s triads contain elements with similar properties; the middle element’s atomic mass is approximately the average of the other two.
rubric.description: Gives a defining feature of the triad: similar properties or the average-mass relationship.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the elements have similar properties or that the middle element’s atomic mass is approximately the average of the other two.

modelAnswer: Dobereiner’s triads are groups of three elements with similar chemical properties.
In a triad, the atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.

items.followUp: How does shielding by inner-shell electrons affect the removal of a valence electron?

rubric.why: Inner-shell electrons shield valence electrons from the nucleus and reduce the effective nuclear attraction.
rubric.description: Explains that shielding reduces the nucleus’s attraction for outer electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding reduces the effective nuclear attraction on valence electrons.

rubric.why: Weaker attraction makes the valence electron easier to remove, allowing a cation to form.
rubric.description: Links reduced attraction to easier electron removal or cation formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that shielding makes electron loss or cation formation easier.

modelAnswer: Inner-shell electrons shield the valence electrons from the attraction of the nucleus.
This reduces the effective nuclear attraction, so a valence electron is removed more easily and a cation forms readily.
